Title: Information Security Analysts
Task: Perform risk assessments and execute tests of data processing system to ensure functioning of data processing activities and security measures.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs can accelerate scoping and documentation-heavy parts of risk assessments and security testing: policy/control mapping to frameworks, generating test plans and evidence request lists, normalizing asset/data-flow inventories, summarizing scan and log outputs, drafting risk narratives and remediation plans. With expert supervision and grounding in org-specific data, these save hours but still require hands-on validation and environment-specific judgment to keep quality equivalent.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: yes. Faulty assessments or tests can enable breaches, outages, or regulatory violations. Using LLMs increases risk by adding new attack surfaces (prompt injection from logs/configs, model supply-chain and API dependencies, tool integrations that can execute or exfiltrate), potential leakage of sensitive architecture/vulnerability data to third parties (privacy), and plausible but wrong findings or prioritization (misinformation) that create false assurance or missed critical issues. Malicious actors can also leverage or target the LLM to evade tests or automate attacks. Relative impact: without strong controls, likelihood of assessment error or data exposure is materially higher—roughly a 1.5–3x increase versus traditional workflows; with strict sandboxing, on-prem inference, least-privilege tool use, PII minimization, and mandatory human review, the incremental risk can be reduced to near baseline but remains non-zero.
